BREAKING NEWS: F3 Driver Jeffz Involved in Fatal Crash in Mexico
MEXICO CITY, Mexico – Tragic news has struck the paddock at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez as Formula 3 driver Jeffz, competing for LM Performance, has passed away following a catastrophic incident on Lap 39 of today's race.

The driver lost control at high speed, triggering a heavy impact against the outer perimeter barriers that immediately burst into a massive, fiery inferno. Smoke and flames engulfed the wreckage, prompting an instant red-flag period.

Emergency crews and trackside firefighters rushed to the scene to extinguish the blaze, but officials have since confirmed that Jeffz succumbed to injuries sustained in the severe impact.

Jeffz, who competed hard throughout the season for LM Performance, leaves behind a remarkable racing legacy. The entire motorsport community and VMS paddock send their deepest condolences to Jeffz's family, friends, and the LM Performance team.

@Goofy Ping

author: Silky | Head of F1, F2 & F3
text:
BREAKING NEWS: VMS Star Lory Involved in Fatal Track Crash
Tragedy struck today at the track as one-time VMS World Drivers' Champion Lory passed away following a dramatic and fiery high-speed accident.

Lory, who secured the VMS World Drivers' Championship title previously, was competing in the final stretch of the season. After a closely fought battle throughout the year, Lory narrowly missed out on securing a second championship title during the final race, finishing as the season runner-up.

Emergency crews and track firefighters responded immediately to the crash site, but officials have confirmed that Lory succumbed to injuries sustained in the severe impact. The VMS racing community and motorsport fans worldwide mourn the loss of a fierce competitor and former world champion.

@Goofy Ping

text:
## BEST RACE IN VMS HISTORY????

The VMS F1 MacMillan Cancer Support Singapore GP was bound to be chaotic, with it being rainy at a street circuit. But what actually happened was unbelievable.

For most of the race, it was @Lory | 🇮🇹 | 1  in P1, @ShadowRex | 🇪🇨 | 26 in P2 and his teammate @Maldonado in 3rd, but they ended up finishing 4th and 7th after some bad strategy calls.

We had 2 Safety Cars, 1 was brought out by @Waffle | 🇰🇷 | 25 and the other @Sly | 🇬🇧 | 48 . Sly had already crashed on the opening laps, so he fell from P2 to about P13, before getting into the points and DNFing.

On the first Safety Car restart, it was mental! @syxe | 🇦🇹 | #34 on his debut managed to get up into P2, before somehow fumbling and finished P5. The second SC restart however, was a 2 lap shootout to the end. It saw @il predestinato | 🇬🇧 | 69 momentarily in P2, before his tires discombobulated themselves and ended the race in P8 on his first race since Qatar. 

@Lory | 🇮🇹 | 1 managed to win in the end, achieving a Grand Slam and his first race win all the way back in Round 4 of Season 0, the days when @LeBron James was Lory’s CEO at Ferrari! But probably the biggest headline of this race were the people in P2 and P3.

Having finished in dead last and **4 laps down** in Brazil, @Unironically | 🇨🇦 | 14 went from starting in the pits (effectively P17), and made some last lap overtakes to take P2, a first podium for Mercedes since Noel in Hungary!

The last podium spot went to @gkf | 🇰🇷 | 27 , who managed to get his, and South Korea’s, first ever podium in VMS. This was also McLarens first podium of the season, their last were the days of @Nick and Michael in Season 0!

@News and Media Ping @Race Ping

text:
## Interview with @Piko | 🇪🇸 | 53 after P3 in Brazil

Silky: Hello Piko, just gonna interview today if thats alright.

Piko: Sure, always happy to be interviewed.

Silky: First up then. How would you say that wet Brazil race was, with lots of penalties and some interesting incidents in the pit lane...?

Piko: Well yeah i have to say in my defence thats since Qatar is not being the same, i have been dealing with depression and a lot of work and things to do from college so i couldnt have that much time to practice, even tho i did a very good qualy, is safe to say that i couldnt practice the ccs that much, and well the pitlane, i tried to practice it in qualy and fp, but it was funny how everyone just went into the wall cause of the nerves of the race.

Silky: Now with Jeffz winning 2 race in a row (on track) do you think your winning the WDC is going to be harder, or will Jeffz pose no threat?

Piko: At the moment im in a kinda difficult relationship with jeffz because of things that were said during last race, but as far as i know, i just need to get 40 points until the end of the season to win the wdc, it will be harder? yeh, but i think that the only posible question is how much more races will pass until I clinch that WDC, and hopefully get the WCC in the few races posible

Silky: Finally, do you think you will be able to win in a (as it stands) wet Singapore GP, and boost your title hopes?

Piko: Realistically i dont think so unless jeffz does very badly, but because i cant practice until the day before, and i have heard of how difficult and strict is in dry, i cant imagine how of a challenge will be in rain, but hey, everything is a challenge who knows? im here to have fun and win after all

Silky: Alright thanks for your time, good luck for the remaining races

Piko: Always glad to help

@News and Media Ping
